Col. Ravinder Pal Singh Brar vs Asian Motors on 28 September, 2007

  
 
 
 
 
 
 IN THE STATE COMMISSION:DELHI
  
 
 
 







 



 

   

 

   

 

   

 

   

 

 IN THE STATE COMMISSION:   DELHI  

 

(Constituted under Section 9 of The Consumer
Protection Act, 1986)

Decision: 28.09.2007

A-71/06

1. Whether Reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2. To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

Justice J.D. Kapoor, President (Oral)  

1. Vide impugned order dated 26.09.2005 passed by the District Forum, the respondents have been directed to replace the engine of the vehicle purchased by the appellant and pay Rs. 5,000/- as compensation alongwith Rs. 1,000/- as cost of complaint. Feeling dissatisfied with the order of replacement of engine as well as compensation of Rs. 5,000/-, the appellant has preferred this appeal.

2. The allegations of the appellant that led to the impugned order were that he purchased a car make Lancer in April, 2003 for Rs. 9,24,379/- from respondent-1 while respondent-2 is the manufacturer.

The delivery of the vehicle was delayed by 20 days after full payment was made. The vehicle in question developed various defects for which various letters were written to respondents regarding the defects viz. engine was consuming too much oil, the battery of the car was of make March, 2002 which was     delivered in April, 2003 the same became dead after four months. Although respondent had changed the battery, poor quality components were used in the vehicle and also there was poor head lights and abnormal sound in the AC etc. The car was shown to respondent various times. It was also found that due to defective car, the tyres of the car were getting spoiled. After perusing the matter with respondent-2 the manufacturer, to rectify the problem of excessive consumption of engine oil and noise in the AC, respondent-2 offered to replace the engine of the car admitting inherent defect in the engine.

However, this offer was refused as it would have reduced the market value of the car. Appellant gave legal notice to respondent for refund of Rs. 17,16,939/- towards the cost of the car, interest and compensation etc.

3. As regards the allegation against the respondent-1, it has denied all the allegations and averred that the car was ready for delivery but the appellant delayed the delivery as he wanted to take the car on 13.04.03 on the occasion of Baisakhi and whenever the vehicle was brought with defects, resulting from normal wear and tear, the same were rectified to the satisfaction of the appellant. Respondent-1 had also denied the allegation of having sold second hand car which was subsequently replaced by a new car. Further that the appellant has used the vehicle for 40,000 kms. and as per the warranty , the car was having warranty for two years or 40,000 kms. whichever was earlier.

4. It is a misconceived notion that unless a brand new vehicle or goods suffers from inherent defect, the same cannot be ordered to be replaced or the defective parts to be replaced. We have taken consistent view in case after case that large number of visits of the consumer to the garage for removing one defect or the other coupled with large number of job cards and that too in few months time after the purchase of vehicle are circumstances enough to brand the vehicle a defective vehicle.

5. On the one hand, the consumer is facing hardship of getting one defect or the other removed by taking the vehicle time and again on every second and third day at the cost of time, and expense and business etc. while on the other hand, if we insist on him to produce an expert to prove inherent defect, it is neither in the interest of the consumer nor as per provision of the Consumer Protection Act. Mere allegation of consumer that the vehicle suffers from manufacturing defect is sufficient unless and until it is contradicted or controverted by the manufacturer by producing the expert evidence.

6. Be that as it may, the quality or standard of the vehicle has to be tested on the anvil of the definition of word defect which means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or (under any contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any good.

7. Again it is a misconception that the warranty has the effect of rendering the defects in the vehicle redundant. The concept of warranty is that the dealer or the manufacturer may charge for removal or rectifying the defects as pointed out after the warranty period. Rather, the circumstance of the vehicle being still taken for removal of defects after the warranty period strengthens the claim of the consumer that the goods were defective and therefore need to be replaced by new goods or the cost be refunded.

8. Engine is the heart and soul of the vehicle. Merely because respondent-2 offered to replace the engine of the vehicle did not absolve it from having manufactured or sold a defective goods. In such a case if owner of the car intends to sell the vehicle after a year or so for purchasing a new vehicle he shall always be encountered by the prospective purchaser that the original engine has been replaced and as such the market value of the vehicle will go down considerably as it will be very difficult to convince the prospective consumer that the original engine was replaced by a brand new engine and no prospective purchaser would touch such a vehicle.

9. We have taken a view that whenever a customer decides to purchase a brand new vehicle or goods at considerably high price and does not choose to have a 2nd hand or 3rd hand vehicle the minimum expectation of a consumer is that he would not face inconvenience or physical discomfort or other kind of financial loss etc. for getting the defects removed every second or third day. Otherwise the very intention of a consumer to go for a very costly brand new vehicle should suffer such a blow that he would undergo immense mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering, physical discomfort and would deem himself as subject of injustice.

10. The pleas which are being oftenly taken by the manufacturers and the dealers are that whenever a consumer has brought the vehicle to it for removing one or other defects including the minor or major defect they have attended to it, does not absolve them from the liability of selling a defective vehicle.

11. In modern day busy life no person has time to take his brand new vehicle every second day to the service centre and undergo inconvenience and miseries of taking such a vehicle. Therefore he needs to be compensated.

12. It was to inculcate the sense of efficiency in service and inculcate quality and standard in the manufacturing of the vehicles and other goods that the legislature brought on the statute book a very stern definition of word defect and the Supreme Court has extended the meaning of compensation vis--vis consumer Protection Act to such a wide extent that it encompasses each and every component including the mental trauma, emotional suffering, inconvenience on day today basis, professional loss and loss of enjoyment of a new vehicle benefit.

   

13. The observations of the Supreme Court in Ghaziabad Development Authority Vs Union of India & Anr. II (2000)CPJ(SC) need to be reproduced and are as under:

i)                    Whether compensation can be awarded for mental agony suffered by the claimants?
ii)                   Whether in the absence of any contract or promise held out by the Ghaziabad Development Authority any amount by way of interest can be directed to be paid on the amount found due and payable by the Authority to the claimants?
iii)                 If, so, the rate at which the interest can be ordered to be paid?
 

14. Answers to all the aforesaid questions were in the affirmative. As to the rate of interest, Supreme Court held that reasonable interest means it should neither be too high nor too low.

15. Thus there is unvarying judicial unanimity that under the provisions of Consumer Protection Act interest can be   awarded by way of compensation where contract does not provide for payment of interest but only when there are equitable grounds and not otherwise. Further that interest should be reasonable which means it should be neither too high nor too low.

16. We have also taken a view that whenever a person purchases new goods which are found to be so defective that these need to be replaced by another new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect, replacement by new vehicle is not a pragmatic solution.

17. In our view, the disputes between the consumer and the service providers and traders should be ended once for all by calling upon the traders and the manufacturers to refund the cost of the vehicle or the goods with adequate compensation as the possibility of the new goods also being defective and not being upto the satisfaction of the consumers, cannot be ruled out and in that case parties will be relegated to square one and will suffer another bout of litigation. Merely because the appellant had run vehicle for 40,000 kms. reluctantly and grudgingly after taking it on number of occasions to the garage does not mean that the     manufacturer of a defective goods can escape from its liability.

18. In the given facts and circumstance of the case, we allow the appeal by modifying the impugned order to the effect that the respondent shall refund the entire cost of the vehicle on its return and in lieu of interest we allow a lump sum compensation of Rs. 2.5 lacs for the mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering, physical discomfort, trauma as we cannot be oblivious of the fact that the appellant had arranged a loan from the bank and had been paying interest.

19. Payment shall be made within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order.

20. Bank Guarantee/FDR if any, furnished by the appellant, be returned forthwith.

21. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record room.

     

22. Copy of this order be sent to Presidents of all the District Forums.

23. Announced on 28th day of September, 2007.

         

(Justice J.D. Kapoor) President       (Rumnita Mittal) Member                     ysc
